name: Hereditary Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia Type 4

criteria.description: Presence of pathogenic or likely pathogenic mutation in the MAX gene
Development of tumors in at least two endocrine glands including parathyroid, pancreas, or adrenal glands
Family history of MEN4 or related endocrine tumors

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Pathogenic MAX gene mutation plus tumors in at least two endocrine glands
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires genetic testing to confirm MAX mutation and clinical evidence of multiple endocrine tumors.

common.symptomName: Abdominal pain due to pancreatic tumors

rare.symptomName: Visual disturbances from pancreatic tumor metastases
Psychiatric symptoms such as anxiety due to catecholamine excess

laboratory: Elevated serum calcium and parathyroid hormone levels
Elevated plasma and urine catecholamines and metanephrines
Elevated pancreatic hormone markers (e.g. insulin, gastrin) depending on tumor type
imaging: Parathyroid ultrasound or sestamibi scan showing adenomas
Abdominal CT/MRI identifying pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors
genetic: Pathogenic variants in the MAX gene confirmed by molecular genetic testing
other: Family history of endocrine tumors consistent with MEN4

distinguishingFeatures: MEN1 gene mutation instead of MAX
Higher prevalence of parathyroid hyperplasia rather than adenomas
Pheochromocytomas more common and earlier onset

redFlags: Rapid onset hypertension with headaches and sweating
Severe hypercalcemia symptoms including confusion and arrhythmias
Multiple endocrine tumors in a young individual with family history
references: Lemos MC, et al. The MAX gene and hereditary pheochromocytoma. Endocr Relat Cancer. 2016.
Marini F, et al. MEN4 syndrome: clinical and genetic features. Endocrine. 2017.
Orphanet: Multiple endocrine neoplasia type 4. Available at: https://www.orpha.net
